summary: Six findings: one high, four medium and one low. The most consequential correction is that the logarithm gap recorded as new and unresolved in E5/E6 has an explicit later repair by Burungale–Skinner–Wan, already public before the extraction's review. Preserve the historical proof omission, import the repair and restore the original conclusions instead of imposing new hypotheses on Theorems A and E. Other findings concern four overwritten statements, an indefinite/definite quaternionic owner mismatch, an unextracted Cassels–Tate input, an application incorrectly marked planned, and inconsistent source metadata. All 78 items, six routes and eleven source issues were checked against the complete published article; every missing item is routed exactly once.
checked: Independent worker Codex, session codex-J6LwjP, issue #4322; neither author nor reviewer of PAPER-SKINNER-20. Repository base 287c773. Read the accepted result, report, paper review result/report, WORKERS.md, PROTOCOL.md including sections 3–4 and 15–18, expansion PROTOCOL.md and UPSTREAM_GUIDE.md.

Read all 26 pages, including references, of Skinner's published article, Annals 191 (2020), 329–354, at https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v191-n2-p01-s.pdf on 2026-09-30. SHA256 cfdfab6e62ac507be40d1f0bc8d9cb8371d95b42c5ae259fde054c70fb20c214. Checked journal metadata and arXiv history separately from later-paper searches.

Checked all 78 items (28 planned, 50 missing), all eleven source issues, thirteen prerequisite records and six routes. Recomputed route coverage: exactly the 50 missing IDs, each once, no extra ID. Checked the twelve named hypotheses, both Heegner cases, strict versus relaxed primes, the implication chain through Lemmas 2.3.1–2.3.2 and Propositions 2.7.2–2.7.3, the two twist-nonvanishing branches, and the published unramified coefficient extension.

Read Burungale–Skinner–Wan, arXiv:2603.20886v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.20886v2, especially sections 1.2–1.4, 2.1–2.2, 3 and 4.1, on 2026-09-30. SHA256 f2b4a020bf5dbcd33df3a4b30cbf27230dc0d0775312f5e543b03b2486f6a994. Inspected the page image of Theorem 1.1 to distinguish Q-bar from Q in the extracted text. The theorem applies to algebraic points, not just Q-rational points; M_f is totally real of degree dim(A_f).

Read the Cassels–Tate statements in the abstract and section 1 of Poonen–Stoll's corrected author version, https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/papers/sha.pdf, on 2026-09-30, SHA256 3b9a619423358bc877fd2123b73a759157a728ec11e0f7b0aa48bd0333d7149a. Kept the elliptic alternating pairing distinct from the more delicate assertion for arbitrary principally polarized abelian varieties.

Resolved all 42 distinct planned stage IDs and read their contracts, plus the source-route stages, R18.1/R18.4, DT.3 and the relevant roadmap documents. Consulted reviewed library-coverage entries for those 42 IDs: 39 entries and three absent entries (R29.5, R29.6, R20.2); did not treat missing audit entries as evidence of implementation. Searched roadmap definitions and packets for Cassels–Tate and analytic-subgroup suppliers; ArithmeticStatistics already records the former as a shared gap.

Confirmed source checkouts at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Searched declarations and source files for Selmer, Iwasawa, Heegner, Bloch–Kato, Cassels–Tate and p-adic analytic subgroup material. Read TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/SelmerGroup.lean:104–123, Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/PontryaginDual.lean:37, Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Ideal.lean:196–202, and TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/StrongMultiplicityOne.lean:87–121. The 2-Selmer construction is not Skinner's odd-p group, and fixed-level strong multiplicity one is not item 73's cross-level conclusion. Existing power-series algebra must be reused, but does not supply characteristic ideals or control.

Investigated the proposed specialization concern in item 41 rather than reporting it as false. Read Skinner–Urban's public author preprint, https://www.math.columbia.edu/~urban/eurp/MC.pdf, sections 3.1.6 and 3.2.7–3.2.10, including Proposition 3.2.8 and Corollary 3.2.9 (this preprint's numbering). SHA256 f9faa40aa5e30eba705da88e3d68c8aa43069b5be01c1cc6ece212dd57879748. The one-sided characteristic-ideal inclusion is compatible with base change via Fitting ideals; it is not an equality claim defeated merely by a pseudo-null specialization term. The arithmetic control comparison remains a separate obligation.

No Lean file is a deliverable, no Lean project or cache was created, and nothing was compiled. Structural validation is recorded in the accompanying report; it does not certify the mathematics. No claim to have read every cited monograph or completely audited every supplier's implementation is made.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SKINNER-20.result.json: sourceIssues E5/E6; items 5, 10, 20, 39, 59, 62, 77; routes[0].brief; research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SKINNER-20.md: final review section
findings.claim: The accepted extraction treats the eigendifferential logarithm input as an unresolved new gap and directs the designer to weaken Theorems A and E in higher dimension. There is an explicit public repair, predating the September review. This is a historical omission in the printed proof, not a currently unknown extra hypothesis for the modular abelian varieties under discussion. E5/E6 and the dependent corrections omit the repair and therefore change the intended theorem unnecessarily.
findings.evidence: Burungale–Skinner–Wan, A refined non-vanishing of the p-adic logarithm of a rational point on an abelian variety, arXiv:2603.20886v2 (10 May 2026), https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.20886v2, section 1.2 explicitly identifies Skinner Lemma 2.2.2 and says 'no proof was given'; it then says 'we supply a proof'. Theorem 1.1, p. 3, applies to A over Q-bar with a field F in End^0(A), dim A=[F:Q] and a real embedding of F: every non-torsion algebraic point has nonzero logarithm for every nonzero F-eigendifferential. Theorem 2.3/Remark 2.4 and section 4.1 prove this using the F-stable analytic subgroup theorem 3.2. For Skinner's A_f, take F=M_f, which is totally real. A rational Mordell–Weil generator then has a nonzero lambda projection; with the rank-one Kummer comparison this supplies Lemma 2.2.2. The Heegner point is obtained from the f-projector of a rational divisor class, so the same result applies to its eigendifferential logarithm. E5 currently says the required nonvanishing is not known in general and E5/E6 have known='new'.
findings.fix: Retain the historical proof omission but change E5/E6 to a documented gap repaired by the exact later source; update their correction, reason, known, searched and dependent explanatory notes consistently. Restore the published conclusions of Lemma 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.6.2 and the full Theorems A/E without the newly imposed lambda-uniqueness/nonvanishing hypothesis. Add separately stated missing inputs for the needed algebraic-point logarithm theorem and its analytic-subgroup prerequisite, with the later paper in prerequisites. Route the general transcendence input as an extension/source request to DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3 and its RM/Heegner application to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9; make RankOneConverse import them. These are proposed additions, not claims that DT.3 already contains the theorem. Explain the passage from a rational divisor point to its epsilon_f projection. Keep Theorem B's explicit hypothesis (e), and keep the warning that an arbitrary nonzero cohomology class need not have nonzero logarithm. Do not import the unrelated higher-rank structural-rank conjecture in section 5 of the later paper.

findings.claim: Four statement fields contain editing instructions instead of the extracted mathematics. Items 5 and 10 start with 'Theorem A as printed' and 'Theorem E as printed'; item 19 starts 'Same statement, with'; item 59 starts 'As printed.' Theorems A/E lack their hypotheses and conclusions, and item 19 has lost the definitions and Kummer exact sequence named by its title. A design consumer cannot reconstruct the contracts from these fields.
findings.evidence: Direct read of the four JSON statement fields. Skinner, published pp. 330 and 351–352, states Theorems A and E with squarefree level, the specified odd-prime local alternatives, rank/finiteness assumptions and analytic-order conclusions. Section 2.2, pp. 337–338, defines W, the p-power Selmer group and Sha, gives 0→A_f(K)⊗Q_p/Z_p→Sel_{p∞}(A_f/K)→Sha(A_f/K)[p∞]→0 and the rational Kummer comparison. Section 3, pp. 350–351, supplies the actual deduction of A. PROTOCOL section 16 requires a statement with every hypothesis, not a pointer to an earlier version of a field.
findings.fix: Replace all four instruction fragments with complete mathematical statements transcribed from the published version. In item 19 define W=V_pA_f/T_pA_f, the local conditions, Sel and Sha and give the exact sequence and finite-S/rational comparisons. In item 59 give the ordinary-prime selection, quadratic-twist nonvanishing, passage to K, application of B and L-factorization argument, referencing numbered items for their full hypotheses. Keep editorial commentary in note fields and incorporate finding 1's later repair rather than retaining obsolete extra hypotheses. Preserve item IDs and update the report to match.

findings.claim: The Case II indefinite Shimura-curve realization is assigned to HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3, whose object is a finite double-coset set for a definite quaternion algebra. That stage cannot supply the curve, its differentials or its Jacobian quotient asserted in this item.
findings.evidence: Skinner section 2.4, Case II, p. 340, uses the quaternion algebra of discriminant N-minus split at the real place and the resulting Shimura curve. The item's own statement says 'indefinite quaternion algebra'. The R18.3 contract is titled 'Definite quaternionic forms' and says 'Define algebraic automorphic forms on the finite double-coset set'. R18.1 explicitly constructs the canonical curve for an algebra split at one real place and distinguishes that from R18.3's finite class set. R18.4 supplies cohomology/Hecke comparisons, GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.3 global transfer with rational structures, and GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.3 the rational automorphic realization, parametrization and differential comparison.
findings.fix: Remove R18.3 as the direct supplier of this indefinite realization. Split the transfer, curve/cohomology realization and quotient/normalization assertions as needed, assigning R17.3, R18.1/R18.4 and GZ.3 respectively. Explicitly retain Brooks section 2.8 for the precise M_f normalization; if any part exceeds those contracts, mark and route that residual comparison rather than leaving 'check' in a note under a blanket planned status. Keep Case II Heegner points imported from HE.1 with only the Skinner-specific normalization adapter in RankOneConverse.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SKINNER-20.result.json: items 61/74, prerequisites and routes[0]; shared supplier SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1–L2
findings.claim: Item 74 explicitly relies on the Cassels–Tate pairing and acknowledges that it is unplanned, but the pairing is never extracted as an item or given a reusable owner/source. Routing the final Selmer implication to the p-converse Part II does not close this shared prerequisite. ArithmeticStatistics independently needs the same pairing, so it should not be newly constructed only inside RankOneConverse.
findings.evidence: Item 74 uses the square-order/symplectic structure of the finite p-primary Sha group to exclude a nonzero finite cyclic Selmer group, and its note says 'The Cassels–Tate pairing ... is itself missing from the atlas'. Poonen–Stoll, corrected author version https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/papers/sha.pdf, section 1, p. 2, recalls the pairing on Sha(E), nondegenerate modulo its maximal divisible subgroup, and says it is 'alternating'. The general principally polarized case requires additional care. SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1–L2 supplies duality and local conditions but does not state this pairing on Sha. research/blueprint/packets/ArithmeticStatistics.json independently records the gap 'Cassels–Tate pairing and its isogeny adjointness'. No item among the 78 gives the pairing's construction or theorem.
findings.fix: Add separate items for the elliptic Cassels–Tate pairing, its maximal-divisible kernel/nondegeneracy and its alternating property, with the finite odd-p square-order consequence used by item 74. Add a public prerequisite source, distinguishing the original Cassels/Tate input from a modern exposition or generalization. Route this as a shared source/extension request to SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1–L2, importing ArithmeticGaloisDuality rather than duplicating it; cross-reference ArithmeticStatistics' existing request. Let items 61/74 and RankOneConverse import the resulting theorem. Do not state alternation for arbitrary principally polarized abelian varieties without the required qualifications, and do not claim Sha is finite before the argument proves it.

findings.claim: The entire deduction of Theorem A-prime from Theorem A is marked planned at EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6. R29.6 supplies modularity and the L-function comparison, but does not plan the p-converse application, isogeny invariance of Sha finiteness or Theorem A. The extraction has mistaken an input for a plan of the whole stated implication.
findings.evidence: Item 64 combines the modular quotient, local-component dictionary, rank/Sha isogeny invariance and Theorem A to obtain A-prime. Its only planned stage, R29.6, says 'Do not claim the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture or a rank formula as a consequence.' Its actual outputs are modularity, parametrization, local-factor comparison, continuation and functional equation. Skinner p. 330 applies the preceding new converse theorem in making this deduction; item 6 and route 1 already assign that converse to RankOneConverse.
findings.fix: Keep the modularity component as an import from R29.5–R29.6 and the local dictionary from item 63's actual suppliers. Mark the assembly item 64 missing and add it exactly once to the existing RankOneConverse route, or split the item into planned inputs and a missing assembly. Record the isogeny-invariance input explicitly alongside the quadratic-descent/Sha comparisons rather than attributing it to modularity. Do not propose another roadmap or extend R29.6 into a p-converse owner.

findings.claim: A few provenance and terminology fields remain inconsistent after the review: Serre's page range is 323–401 rather than 123–201; the Wan prerequisite and item 47 retain the preprint's Sigma,Hida notation without a version dictionary, while item 46 uses the published Sigma notation but its note says it uses the preprint notation; the report's routing paragraph calls the p-strict/p-bar-relaxed group p-relaxed.
findings.evidence: Skinner's published bibliography, p. 353, reference [23], gives Serre, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 54 (1981), 123–201; the prerequisite URL itself contains 123. Published p. 346 writes the two-variable function with superscript Sigma and references Wan section 7.5, whereas arXiv:1405.7294v1 p. 16 uses Sigma,Hida and section 6. Section 2.3, p. 339, imposes the vanishing restriction at the displayed prime p and permits the other p-adic place; the accepted item 49 note already explains this distinction. These discrepancies are in descriptive fields, not new failures of the mathematics.
findings.fix: Correct Serre's page range; use the published Wan notation consistently or provide one explicit preprint-to-publication dictionary, removing the stale note on item 46. Correct the routing brief/report to say strict at p and relaxed at p-bar. Keep the useful source-version comparison and the published unramified coefficient rings.
